rv.q: A masterful interpretation of a musical theatre classic, bursting with talent, imagination and theatrical magic.
It's a musically sumptuous feast crammed full of ambition, enthusiasm and botanical bad behaviour, with Audrey II stealing the show every time she opens her lascivious mouth to bitch or bite.
It's just a joyful night at the theatre. I had a grin on my face for the whole time and perhaps a few tears, some for the fate of the characters, some just for the beauty of the writing.
Six choreographer Carrie-Anne Ingrouille brings fresh bite to this cult classic
With its infectious score and sharp humour, this production is one that understands exactly what makes this musical so enduring.
Overall, this production is a triumph perfectly scaled to the intimacy of the Hope Mill Theatre, though it would imaginably delight audiences on a larger stage as well.
The cult horror-comedy musical is back at Manchester's Hope Mill Theatre, and it's an absolute blast.

cn.t: This cult horror-comedy musical delights critics with its bloodthirsty plant star and gloriously sadistic performances, particularly Benjamin Yates as the dentist, delivering a darkly comic blast that has audiences grinning throughout.
